stories.title: 1954 Atomic Energy Act moved craft custody to contractor-operated labs

tellings.quote: different mind. I think that craft was moved in 1954 because the 1954 atomic energy agreement gave expanded powers to government-owned contractor operated laboratories like Sandia and so forth to house the craft.

To the extent deemed necessary, the Commission is authorized to make, or to continue in effect, contracts with persons obligating them to produce special nuclear material in facilities owned by the Commission.

discussion.by: Atomic Energy Act of 1954 (Public Law 703, 83rd Congress, 68 Stat. 919)
discussion.text: The teller does not say which provision of the 1954 act he means; if it is section 41 b., the act says "the Commission is authorized to make, or to continue in effect, contracts with persons obligating them to produce special nuclear material in facilities owned by the Commission", and lets it enter "research and development contracts" for work in those facilities, the government-owned, contractor-operated arrangement the teller describes. The act speaks of producing nuclear material and of research there; that such facilities were given a craft to hold, and that this is why a craft moved in 1954, is the teller's step, which the act neither states nor excludes.

documents.title: The King James Version of the Bible

discussion.by: The King James Version of the Bible
discussion.text: In the King James Version, Genesis tells that God "created man in his own image", that "the LORD God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life", and that he made the woman from a rib he took from Adam during "a deep sleep", a making of the first humans by a higher hand. Reading that making as genetic work done on beings already living is the teller's step, which the text neither states nor excludes.

And Nadab and Abihu, the sons of Aaron, took either of them his censer, and put fire therein, and put incense thereon, and offered strange fire before the LORD, which he commanded them not.
And there went out fire from the LORD, and devoured them, and they died before the LORD.

documents.title: The King James Version of the Bible

discussion.by: The King James Version of the Bible
discussion.text: The books of Moses tell of a deadly holiness about the Ark: when Aaron's sons offered strange fire, "there went out fire from the LORD, and devoured them" (Leviticus 10:2), and Aaron is warned to keep from "the mercy seat, which is upon the ark; that he die not" (Leviticus 16:2). The books of Samuel, which name no author, tell of deaths at the Ark itself: Uzzah, who "died by the ark of God" when God "smote him" (2 Samuel 6:7), and the men of Bethshemesh smitten "because they had looked into the ark of the LORD" (1 Samuel 6:19). So a deadly Ark is in the text, and so is fire from the LORD; the passages are in Leviticus and Samuel where the teller names Exodus, and joining the two into fire coming out of the Ark itself is the teller's step, which the text neither states nor excludes.

discussion.text: In the Revelation, Armageddon is the place where the kings of the earth are gathered "to the battle of that great day of God Almighty" (16:14, 16:16); the war against the rider on the white horse, whose "name is called The Word of God", is told in chapter 19, where the kings and their armies are "gathered together to make war against him that sat on the horse", and the remnant are slain "with the sword of him that sat upon the horse, which sword proceeded out of his mouth" (19:21). I saw in my sleep what I will now say with a tongue of flesh and with the breath of my mouth: which the Great One has given to men to converse therewith and understand with the heart.

And the vision was shown to me thus: Behold, in the vision clouds invited me and a mist summoned me, and the course of the stars and the lightnings sped and =hastened= me, and the winds in the vision caused me to fly and lifted me upward, and bore me into heaven.
And I went in till I drew nigh to a wall which is built of crystals and surrounded by tongues of fire: and it began to affright me.

And I went into the tongues of fire and drew nigh to a large house which was built of crystals: and the walls of the house were like a tesselated floor (made) of crystals, and its groundwork was of crystal.
And lo! there was a second house, greater than the former, and the entire portal stood open before me, and it was built of flames of fire.
And I looked and saw 〚therein〛 a lofty throne: its appearance was as crystal, and the wheels thereof as the shining sun, and there was the =vision= of cherubim.

documents.title: The Book of Enoch (translated by R. H. Charles)

discussion.by: The Book of Enoch (translated by R. H. Charles)
discussion.text: In the Book of Enoch the ascent comes in a vision in sleep ("I saw in my sleep", 14:2), in which "the winds in the vision caused me to fly and lifted me upward, and bore me into heaven" (14:8): Enoch passes "a wall which is built of crystals", enters "a large house which was built of crystals", and then sees "a second house, greater than the former", holding a throne whose wheels shine "as the shining sun" (14:9 to 18). The book tells two houses, not seven palaces, and has Enoch carried up by the winds of the vision rather than rising by breathing, visualisation or prayer. The teller names the Merkavah texts beside it; joining their seven palaces and their practices to Enoch's ascent is the teller's reading, which this book neither states nor excludes.

discussion.by: Critias (translated by Benjamin Jowett)
discussion.text: In Jowett's translation of the Critias, the Atlanteans' fault is that "the divine portion began to fade away" in them and they grew "full of avarice and unrighteous power", where the teller names their ceasing to sacrifice to the gods; Zeus, "wanting to inflict punishment on them, that they might be chastened and improve", calls the gods together, and the text breaks off as he begins to speak, so what he decided is not in it. A flood sent for that fault is the teller's completion of the story, and calling it Noah's flood is his comparison; the text neither states nor excludes either.

discussion.by: Timaeus (translated by Benjamin Jowett)
discussion.text: In Jowett's translation of the Timaeus, Atlantis sank when "violent earthquakes and floods" came "in a single day and night of misfortune", after its war with Athens, and the Athenian warriors sank into the earth with it; the passage tells the sinking without its cause. The cause is told in the Critias, where Zeus calls the gods together to punish the Atlanteans' decline, and joining the two dialogues into a flood sent for a rebellion is a reading they invite, its last step, from punishment to flood, the teller's.

discussion.by: Atomic Energy Act of 1954 (Public Law 703, 83rd Congress, 68 Stat. 919)
discussion.text: The tellers' "born secret" is the common name for what the Act sets up: it defines Restricted Data as "all data concerning (1) design, manufacture, or utilization of atomic weapons; (2) the production of special nuclear material; or (3) the use of special nuclear material in the production of energy", restricted by its subject from the moment it exists, with the Commission charged "to control the dissemination and declassification of Restricted Data". Special nuclear material is plutonium and enriched uranium "and any other material which the Commission, pursuant to the provisions of section 51, determines to be special nuclear material", a determination the Commission may make only after finding the material "capable of releasing substantial quantities of atomic energy", and for which "the President must have expressly assented in writing to the determination"; Grusch's "any material that releases any kind of atomic energy" gives that clause without the finding and the assent. The gap is one of scope: the Act speaks of data and of nuclear materials, and reaching a recovered craft through the "other material" clause is the tellers' extension, which the text neither states nor excludes.

discussion.by: United States Code, 42 U.S.C. 2071 (Cornell Legal Information Institute)
discussion.text: The statute as it stands today lets the Commission add other material to special nuclear material only after finding it capable of releasing substantial quantities of atomic energy, says "the President must have expressly assented in writing to the determination", and has the determination and the assent sent to Congress's Energy Committees, with thirty days of session to pass, before it takes effect. The NRC is quoted in search results as saying it "has not declared any other material as special nuclear material", and no assent under the section is in the open record; the Justice Department's Office of Legal Counsel holds of presidential acts in general that they "remain effective upon a change in administration" until a later president acts, so an early written assent, had one been given, would stand until revoked. The open record holds no case of a president refused access to a special access program; it holds Clinton's remark in Belfast in 1995 that if the Air Force recovered alien bodies "they didn't tell me about it, either", Grusch's sworn statement of 2023 that he himself was "denied access" to the program's read-ons, and laws of 2022 and 2023 that require such programs to be reported to Congress's committees and congressional leadership, naming no role for the President, and no public document found classes recovered craft as special nuclear material.

documents.title: Eisenhower briefing document (MJ-12, 1952)
documents.provenance: A typed briefing paper dated 18 November 1952, with a Truman memorandum to Secretary Forrestal of 24 September 1947 as its Attachment A, that came to light on a roll of 35mm film Jaime Shandera received anonymously at his Burbank home in 1984 and that he, William Moore and Stanton Friedman then studied; it was made public in 1987. The National Archives and the Truman and Eisenhower Libraries report their searches for it negative. The FBI's Majestic 12 file holds copies sent to it in 1988 and 1991, each marked "BOGUS" by hand, and records that the Air Force Office of Special Investigations "advised on November 30, 1988, that the document was fabricated" and that "the document is completely bogus". Philip Klass called the Truman memo an obvious fraud; Friedman judged the briefing paper and the memo "almost certainly genuine".

discussion.text: In the report's own figure of evaluations the unknowns are "Unknown 434=19.7%" of 2,199 object sightings, within 3,201 sighting reports in all; the teller's "21%" is near that share, while his count of "almost a thousand" cases is none of the report's bases. The report itself concludes that "the probability that any of the UNKNOWNS considered in this study are "flying saucers'' is concluded to be extremely small" and that it is "highly improbable" that any report shows "technological developments outside the range of present-day scientific knowledge": the step from its data table to a finding the press release hid is the teller's reading, set against the report's own conclusion.

discussion.by: The King James Version of the Bible
discussion.text: Genesis 6 holds the core of the story in a few verses: "the sons of God saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives", and "There were giants in the earth in those days", when "the sons of God came in unto the daughters of men". The Watchers, their number and Mount Hermon belong to the Book of Enoch's fuller telling, which the tellers name; reading Genesis's sons of God as those same beings is the step the tellers take with Enoch, which the short Genesis passage neither states nor excludes.

discussion.by: CIA's Role in the Study of UFOs, 1947-90
discussion.text: The teller credits Project Blue Book without naming a record. Gerald Haines's history of the CIA's role in the study of UFOs, published by the CIA in 1997, says that in 1952 the CIA formed "a special study group within the Office of Scientific Intelligence (OSI)", that Edward Tauss, reporting for the group, urged "that CIA conceal its interest from the media and the public", and that the Air Force's ATIC "tried to persuade the public that UFOs were not extraordinary"; a hidden CIA interest beside a public Air Force effort is close to what the teller calls taking the research underground. That Blue Book served as a cover or a psychological operation for that hidden work is the teller's step, which the history neither states nor excludes.

discussion.by: Report of Meetings of Scientific Advisory Panel on Unidentified Flying Objects (Robertson Panel), 14-18 January 1953
discussion.text: The tellers do not say which of the panel's papers they mean; if it is the minutes and report read here (the declassified text printed as Appendix U of the Condon report), the panel names the "Civilian Flying Saucer Investigators" and the "Aerial Phenomena Research Organization" and says such organizations "should be watched because of their potentially great influence on mass thinking" and that "the possible use of such groups for subversive purposes should be kept in mind", an official recommendation to keep watch on named civilian groups. The step from watched to infiltrated is the tellers' reading, which the report as released neither confirms nor excludes. As context, not as evidence: how a watch was to be kept is the kind of thing such minutes rarely set down.

discussion.text: The report says the Air Force paid for the project ("The first research contract with AFOSR provided $313,000 for the first 15 months"), that the contract provided that its "planning, direction and conclusions" were to be "conducted wholly independently of the Air Force", and that "the Air Force was ordered to furnish the project with the records of its own earlier work and to provide the support of personnel at AF bases when requested by our field teams", a working tie the report itself sets out. discussion.by: Timaeus (translated by Benjamin Jowett)
discussion.text: Where the tellers call the Atlantis story a myth or a lie, in Jowett's translation of the Timaeus Critias calls it "a tale which, though strange, is certainly true" and Socrates repeats that it is "not a mere legend, but an actual fact". The festival in the text is the Apaturia, at which the elder Critias, nearly ninety, told the tale when the younger Critias was about ten; the younger retells it on the day of the goddess's festival.

discussion.by: Elite Officer Recalls Bin Laden Hunt (60 Minutes)
discussion.text: In the 60 Minutes report of October 2008, Dalton Fury says two of Delta's plans against bin Laden at Tora Bora (coming over the mountains from the Pakistan side, and mining the passes into Pakistan) were disapproved by higher headquarters; the report does not speak of having bin Laden in sight three times or of overwatch, and it says that on the night his team was about 2,000 meters from where they thought bin Laden was, Fury himself decided not to advance.

documents.title: Eisenhower briefing document (MJ-12, 1952)
documents.provenance: A typed briefing paper dated 18 November 1952, with a Truman memorandum to Secretary Forrestal of 24 September 1947 as its Attachment A, that came to light on a roll of 35mm film Jaime Shandera received anonymously at his Burbank home in 1984 and that he, William Moore and Stanton Friedman then studied; it was made public in 1987. The National Archives and the Truman and Eisenhower Libraries report their searches for it negative. The FBI's Majestic 12 file holds copies sent to it in 1988 and 1991, each marked "BOGUS" by hand, and records that the Air Force Office of Special Investigations "advised on November 30, 1988, that the document was fabricated" and that "the document is completely bogus". Philip Klass called the Truman memo an obvious fraud; Friedman judged the briefing paper and the memo "almost certainly genuine".

discussion.by: Eisenhower briefing document (MJ-12, 1952)
discussion.text: A typed briefing paper dated 18 November 1952, with a Truman memorandum to Secretary Forrestal of 24 September 1947 as its Attachment A, that came to light on a roll of 35mm film Jaime Shandera received anonymously at his Burbank home in 1984 and that he, William Moore and Stanton Friedman then studied; it was made public in 1987. The National Archives and the Truman and Eisenhower Libraries report their searches for it negative. The FBI's Majestic 12 file holds copies sent to it in 1988 and 1991, each marked "BOGUS" by hand, and records that the Air Force Office of Special Investigations "advised on November 30, 1988, that the document was fabricated" and that "the document is completely bogus". Philip Klass called the Truman memo an obvious fraud; Friedman judged the briefing paper and the memo "almost certainly genuine". The briefing paper lists "Dr. Detlev Bronk" among the twelve members and gives him more than a name: "A similar analysis of the four dead occupants was arranged by Dr. Bronk", and "Dr. Bronk's team has suggested the term "Extra-terrestrial Biological Entities", or "EBEs"". Michels reports the naming as the paper makes it; Bronk's membership and his team's work hold only as far as the paper is genuine.

discussion.text: An unsigned report that Michael Shellenberger delivered to Congress and Rep. Nancy Mace entered into the record of the House Oversight hearing of 13 November 2024 as a document from the Pentagon; it calls itself the public version of a Defense Department employee's report, cleared for release by the State Department; Matthew Brown, a former Defense Department official, later said he wrote it; and a Defense Department spokesperson said the department has no record of a program by that name. The report says its author "obtained access to this information while pursuing their lawful duties as an employee of the Department of Defense" and gives the program's mission as "collecting imagery intelligence on Unidentified Aerial Phenomena (UAP) and ARV/RV (Reproduction Vehicles) utilizing tasked and untasked U.S. military-intelligence resources", in "a global surveillance and reconnaissance mission". Matthew Brown tells of the briefing he found, which is not public, and later said he wrote the report as a summary of it, so the report and his account are one source told twice.

tellings.quote: On March 16, 1967, ten Minuteman-I nuclear missiles operated by Malmstrom Air Force Base, Montana, suddenly malfunctioned one after the other, just as a “large round object” was reported to be hovering “directly over” one of them—according to retired USAF Col. Walter Figel, one of two launch officers on duty at Echo Flight during the incident.

Figel received the startling news while in the flight's underground launch control center, via a two-way radio call from an Air Force security guard posted at the missile silo in question. Although skeptical, then-Lt. Figel dispatched a couple of two-man Security Alert Teams to the field to investigate. They subsequently confirmed the presence of the UFO.

In an earlier conversation with me, Carlson himself claimed to have no recollection of a UFO report during the full-flight missile shutdown and further claimed that he recalled no mention of UFOs during the debriefing.

documents.title: The Echo and Oscar Flight Incidents

discussion.by: The Echo and Oscar Flight Incidents
discussion.text: Hastings writes that ten missiles "suddenly malfunctioned one after the other, just as a “large round object” was reported to be hovering “directly over” one of them", on the word of the deputy launch officer, Walter Figel; he also records that the missile commander, Eric Carlson, "claimed to have no recollection of a UFO report during the full-flight missile shutdown", a claim Hastings disputes. The tellers give the UFO report without the commander's dissent, which the article keeps.

tellings.quote: Importantly, other persons have substantiated Col. Figel's account of a UFO-presence during the Echo Flight incident. The late Robert J. Kaminski unequivocally states that his team could find no prosaic cause for the failures.

Kaminski further says that the Air Force interrupted his investigation in mid-stream and ordered him not to file a report on the full-flight shutdown—an unprecedented and still-unexplained development.

discussion.by: Immaculate Constellation report (anonymous, entered into the House Oversight hearing record, 13 November 2024)
discussion.text: An unsigned report that Michael Shellenberger delivered to Congress and Rep. Nancy Mace entered into the record of the House Oversight hearing of 13 November 2024 as a document from the Pentagon; it calls itself the public version of a Defense Department employee's report, cleared for release by the State Department; Matthew Brown, a former Defense Department official, later said he wrote it; and a Defense Department spokesperson said the department has no record of a program by that name. The report names Luis Elizondo twice: the program was "established following the public disclosure of the AATIP/AAWSAP programs by Luis Elizondo in 2017", and internal records "confirm the claims of Mr. Lue Elizondo regarding AATIP/AAWSAP's mission, activities, and findings". Both tie him to AATIP; whether he was read into Immaculate Constellation itself is the question Rep. Nancy Mace put to him at the hearing, and the report does not take it up.

stories.title: Ellsworth radar-jet chase and Bismarck lights
stories.place_text: Ellsworth AFB, South Dakota and Bismarck, North Dakota

tellings.quote: On August 5th, 1953, a trained civilian spotter calls into the base.
The initial incident in this chain of UFO sightings was the sighting by a GOC (Ground Observers Corps) observer of a stationary "red glowing light" at 2005 LST near Blackhawk, S. Dak.
The report was relayed to the Rapid City Filter Center, and three airmen from the radar site were sent outside to look for the UFO.

An F-84 fighter was vectored in to a stationary blip near Blackhawk, and the pilot "chased" a UFO which he found at the location on a heading of 320 ° M. without gaining on it. The F-84 was probably chasing a star, in this case Pollux (mag. 1.2) which was in the correct location (335° true azimuth, near the horizon).

In summary, the Rapid City-Bismarck sightings appear to have been caused by a combination of: stars seen through an inversion layer, at least one meteor, AP echoes on a GCI radar, and possible ghost echoes on the GCI radar and malfunction of an airborne radar gunsight (although the commanding officer of the Rapid City detachment was later skeptical that there had in fact ever been even a ghost echo present on the GCI radar).

documents.title: The Book of Enoch (translated by R. H. Charles)

discussion.by: The Book of Enoch (translated by R. H. Charles)
discussion.text: The Book of Enoch tells that Enoch was "raised aloft on the chariots of the spirit" (70:2); in his own words, "he translated my spirit into the heaven of heavens" (71:5), where "my whole body became relaxed, And my spirit was transfigured" (71:11). Enoch becoming the angel Metatron is told in 3 Enoch, a later Hebrew book of the Hekhalot literature; the step from the transfigured Enoch of this book to the angel Metatron is that later book's, which this book neither states nor excludes, and the teller tells it as the Book of Enoch's.

tellings.quote: On October 23, 2010, F.E. Warren Air Force Base, in Cheyenne, Wyoming, temporarily lost the ability to communicate with 50 of its Minuteman III nuclear missiles. The five Missile Alert Facilities responsible for launching those ICBMs in time of war—Alpha through Echo, comprising the 319th Strategic Missile Squadron—would have been unable to do so during the period of the disruption.
The Air Force then quickly acknowledged the problem, saying that a back-up system could have launched the missiles and claiming that the breakdown had lasted a mere 59 minutes.

However, the latter statement was untrue, according to two missile technicians stationed at F.E. Warren, who say that the communications problem, while intermittent, actually persisted over several hours.

discussion.text: Hastings writes that on 23 and 24 October 2010 "one or more “huge” cigar-shaped objects were observed by active duty Air Force personnel in the field", which a retired technician put at about seven times as long as wide, likened to a Zeppelin; and that the outage "actually persisted over several hours", where the Air Force said 59 minutes. He adds: "I emphasize that the aforementioned confidential sources at the base have not said that the UFO(s) sighted actually caused the disruption", and that Global Strike Command attributed it to "an improperly-replaced circuit card". The object in this article is a huge, Zeppelin-like craft where the tellers speak of a Tic Tac, and the step from an object seen on the day of the outage to the object behind it is the tellers' reading, which Hastings says his sources did not make.

documents.title: Eisenhower briefing document (MJ-12, 1952)
documents.provenance: A typed briefing paper dated 18 November 1952, with a Truman memorandum to Secretary Forrestal of 24 September 1947 as its Attachment A, that came to light on a roll of 35mm film Jaime Shandera received anonymously at his Burbank home in 1984 and that he, William Moore and Stanton Friedman then studied; it was made public in 1987. The National Archives and the Truman and Eisenhower Libraries report their searches for it negative. The FBI's Majestic 12 file holds copies sent to it in 1988 and 1991, each marked "BOGUS" by hand, and records that the Air Force Office of Special Investigations "advised on November 30, 1988, that the document was fabricated" and that "the document is completely bogus". Philip Klass called the Truman memo an obvious fraud; Friedman judged the briefing paper and the memo "almost certainly genuine".

documents.title: Eisenhower briefing document (MJ-12, 1952)
documents.provenance: A typed briefing paper dated 18 November 1952, with a Truman memorandum to Secretary Forrestal of 24 September 1947 as its Attachment A, that came to light on a roll of 35mm film Jaime Shandera received anonymously at his Burbank home in 1984 and that he, William Moore and Stanton Friedman then studied; it was made public in 1987. The National Archives and the Truman and Eisenhower Libraries report their searches for it negative. The FBI's Majestic 12 file holds copies sent to it in 1988 and 1991, each marked "BOGUS" by hand, and records that the Air Force Office of Special Investigations "advised on November 30, 1988, that the document was fabricated" and that "the document is completely bogus". Philip Klass called the Truman memo an obvious fraud; Friedman judged the briefing paper and the memo "almost certainly genuine".

discussion.by: Eisenhower briefing document (MJ-12, 1952)
discussion.text: A typed briefing paper dated 18 November 1952, with a Truman memorandum to Secretary Forrestal of 24 September 1947 as its Attachment A, that came to light on a roll of 35mm film Jaime Shandera received anonymously at his Burbank home in 1984 and that he, William Moore and Stanton Friedman then studied; it was made public in 1987. The National Archives and the Truman and Eisenhower Libraries report their searches for it negative. The FBI's Majestic 12 file holds copies sent to it in 1988 and 1991, each marked "BOGUS" by hand, and records that the Air Force Office of Special Investigations "advised on November 30, 1988, that the document was fabricated" and that "the document is completely bogus". Philip Klass called the Truman memo an obvious fraud; Friedman judged the briefing paper and the memo "almost certainly genuine". Attachment A, the Truman memorandum dated 24 September 1947, is addressed "MEMORANDUM FOR THE SECRETARY OF DEFENSE Dear Secretary Forrestal:" and opens "As per our recent conversati[[on]] on this matt[[er]]" (double brackets mark letters hidden by the stroke on the FBI's one copy); the briefing paper says the group was "established by special classified executive order of President Truman on 24 September, 1947, upon recommendation by Dr. Vannevar Bush and Secretary James Forrestal." The papers give the date and a recent conversation; that the date matches a meeting of the two men is the tellers' comparison with the record of their appointments, which the papers do not hold and neither confirm nor exclude.

discussion.by: The Epic of Gilgamish, Tablet XI (translated by E. A. Wallis Budge in The Babylonian Story of the Deluge)
discussion.text: In the introduction to The Babylonian Story of the Deluge, Budge writes that the tablets "discovered by Layard and Rassam at Nineveh came to the British Museum in 1854-5", that the Trustees "employed George Smith" in 1866 to sort and rejoin them, that he found among them the Gilgamish tablets and the Deluge account, published in December 1872, and that "During the excavations which Smith carried out at Kuyûnjik in 1873 and 1874 he recovered many fragments" before he died in 1876. In this account the first tablets reached the museum through Layard and Rassam, and Smith's own finds at Nineveh are the further fragments of 1873 and 1874; the teller's picture of Smith bringing the tablets to the museum fits those later fragments, not the collection he first read. His years on the tablets run from 1866 to 1876, close to the teller's ten.

documents.title: Eisenhower briefing document (MJ-12, 1952)
documents.provenance: A typed briefing paper dated 18 November 1952, with a Truman memorandum to Secretary Forrestal of 24 September 1947 as its Attachment A, that came to light on a roll of 35mm film Jaime Shandera received anonymously at his Burbank home in 1984 and that he, William Moore and Stanton Friedman then studied; it was made public in 1987. The National Archives and the Truman and Eisenhower Libraries report their searches for it negative. The FBI's Majestic 12 file holds copies sent to it in 1988 and 1991, each marked "BOGUS" by hand, and records that the Air Force Office of Special Investigations "advised on November 30, 1988, that the document was fabricated" and that "the document is completely bogus". Philip Klass called the Truman memo an obvious fraud; Friedman judged the briefing paper and the memo "almost certainly genuine".

discussion.by: Eisenhower briefing document (MJ-12, 1952)
discussion.text: A typed briefing paper dated 18 November 1952, with a Truman memorandum to Secretary Forrestal of 24 September 1947 as its Attachment A, that came to light on a roll of 35mm film Jaime Shandera received anonymously at his Burbank home in 1984 and that he, William Moore and Stanton Friedman then studied; it was made public in 1987. The National Archives and the Truman and Eisenhower Libraries report their searches for it negative. The FBI's Majestic 12 file holds copies sent to it in 1988 and 1991, each marked "BOGUS" by hand, and records that the Air Force Office of Special Investigations "advised on November 30, 1988, that the document was fabricated" and that "the document is completely bogus". Philip Klass called the Truman memo an obvious fraud; Friedman judged the briefing paper and the memo "almost certainly genuine". The briefing paper calls Majestic-12 "a TOP SECRET Research and Development/ Intelligence operation responsible directly and only to the President of the United States" and lists "Mr. Gordon Gray" among the members of the group Truman's order of 24 September 1947 established. Michels' "advisers" is his word for those members; the naming is the paper's, and Gray's part holds only as far as the paper is genuine.

Nancy Mace entered into the record of the House Oversight hearing of 13 November 2024 as a document from the Pentagon; it calls itself the public version of a Defense Department employee's report, cleared for release by the State Department; Matthew Brown, a former Defense Department official, later said he wrote it; and a Defense Department spokesperson said the department has no record of a program by that name.

discussion.by: Immaculate Constellation report (anonymous, entered into the House Oversight hearing record, 13 November 2024)
discussion.text: An unsigned report that Michael Shellenberger delivered to Congress and Rep. Nancy Mace entered into the record of the House Oversight hearing of 13 November 2024 as a document from the Pentagon; it calls itself the public version of a Defense Department employee's report, cleared for release by the State Department; Matthew Brown, a former Defense Department official, later said he wrote it; and a Defense Department spokesperson said the department has no record of a program by that name. The report calls itself a "public version of the author's report", reviewed and approved for release by the State Department, and the copy on Rep. Nancy Mace's House site has 11 unnumbered pages where Mace told the hearing it had 12. Neither the copy nor the hearing record says what the fuller version held, so a missing page bearing Jeremy Corbell's name rests on the tellers' account.

discussion.by: Atomic Energy Act of 1954 (Public Law 703, 83rd Congress, 68 Stat. 919)
discussion.text: The teller does not say which part of the 1954 act he means; if it is its secrecy rules, the act defines Restricted Data as "all data concerning (1) design, manufacture, or utilization of atomic weapons; (2) the production of special nuclear material; or (3) the use of special nuclear material in the production of energy" and makes it the Commission's policy "to control the dissemination and declassification of Restricted Data in such a manner as to assure the common defense and security", a secrecy regime built for atomic data. That the classification and controls of UFO legacy programs grew from that regime is the teller's step, which the act neither states nor excludes.

documents.title: Cutler-Twining memo (MJ-12, 14 July 1954)
documents.provenance: A one-page memorandum dated 14 July 1954 from Robert Cutler to General Nathan Twining that Jaime Shandera and William Moore reported finding in July 1985 in Record Group 341, Entry 267, at the National Archives. The Archives says it "poses problems": the series is filed by Top Secret register number and it bears none; its marking "Top Secret Restricted Information" came into use at the National Security Council only under Nixon; it has no letterhead or watermark; the NSC minutes hold no meeting on 16 July 1954; and Cutler was abroad on 14 July 1954. Stanton Friedman judged it "almost certainly genuine", answering that Cutler had left instructions with NSC executive secretary James Lay. The FBI's Majestic 12 file holds a copy marked "BOGUS" by hand.

documents.title: Eisenhower briefing document (MJ-12, 1952)
documents.provenance: A typed briefing paper dated 18 November 1952, with a Truman memorandum to Secretary Forrestal of 24 September 1947 as its Attachment A, that came to light on a roll of 35mm film Jaime Shandera received anonymously at his Burbank home in 1984 and that he, William Moore and Stanton Friedman then studied; it was made public in 1987. The National Archives and the Truman and Eisenhower Libraries report their searches for it negative. The FBI's Majestic 12 file holds copies sent to it in 1988 and 1991, each marked "BOGUS" by hand, and records that the Air Force Office of Special Investigations "advised on November 30, 1988, that the document was fabricated" and that "the document is completely bogus". Philip Klass called the Truman memo an obvious fraud; Friedman judged the briefing paper and the memo "almost certainly genuine".

The paper is headed "OPERATION MAJESTIC-12 PRELIMINARY BRIEFING FOR PRESIDENT-ELECT EISENHOWER" and "DOCUMENT PREPARED 18 NOVEMBER, 1952", and its page 3 says that on 07 July 1947 "a secret operation was begun to assure recovery of the wreckage of this object for scientific study" and that "four small human-like beings had apparently ejected from the craft at some point before it exploded". tellings.quote: Shortly after the Echo event, a second large-scale, UFO-related ICBM shutdown incident occurred at another of Malmstrom's missile flights, Oscar, according to former Capt. Robert Salas and now-retired Col. Frederick Meiwald, who were the launch officers on duty when it happened.

A short time later, the guard called again and screamed into the phone that a large, glowing, orange-colored, oval-shaped object had suddenly appeared and was silently hovering over the Oscar Launch Control Facility.

Salas quickly woke then-Capt. Meiwald, who was on his rest break, but before he could tell him about the phone calls with the topside guard, they were both shocked to see multiple warning lights indicating the missiles were dropping off alert status—they were malfunctioning.

During a tape-recorded telephone conversation in August 1996, Meiwald, by then a retired colonel, told Salas that shortly after the missiles failed—he remembered six-to-eight, whereas Salas recalls all ten going offline—a two-man security team had been ordered into the field in response to an intrusion alarm at one of the silos.

discussion.by: The Echo and Oscar Flight Incidents
discussion.text: In The Echo and Oscar Flight Incidents (2012), Hastings, telling Salas's account, writes that the guard reported "a large, glowing, orange-colored, oval-shaped object" "silently hovering over the Oscar Launch Control Facility", and that of the missiles that went off alert Meiwald "remembered six-to-eight, whereas Salas recalls all ten going offline". The object is orange in this telling where the tellers say red, and the whole flight of ten is Salas's recollection, which his commander's differs from.

documents.title: Eisenhower briefing document (MJ-12, 1952)
documents.provenance: A typed briefing paper dated 18 November 1952, with a Truman memorandum to Secretary Forrestal of 24 September 1947 as its Attachment A, that came to light on a roll of 35mm film Jaime Shandera received anonymously at his Burbank home in 1984 and that he, William Moore and Stanton Friedman then studied; it was made public in 1987. The National Archives and the Truman and Eisenhower Libraries report their searches for it negative. The FBI's Majestic 12 file holds copies sent to it in 1988 and 1991, each marked "BOGUS" by hand, and records that the Air Force Office of Special Investigations "advised on November 30, 1988, that the document was fabricated" and that "the document is completely bogus". Philip Klass called the Truman memo an obvious fraud; Friedman judged the briefing paper and the memo "almost certainly genuine".

discussion.by: Eisenhower briefing document (MJ-12, 1952)
discussion.text: A typed briefing paper dated 18 November 1952, with a Truman memorandum to Secretary Forrestal of 24 September 1947 as its Attachment A, that came to light on a roll of 35mm film Jaime Shandera received anonymously at his Burbank home in 1984 and that he, William Moore and Stanton Friedman then studied; it was made public in 1987. The National Archives and the Truman and Eisenhower Libraries report their searches for it negative. The FBI's Majestic 12 file holds copies sent to it in 1988 and 1991, each marked "BOGUS" by hand, and records that the Air Force Office of Special Investigations "advised on November 30, 1988, that the document was fabricated" and that "the document is completely bogus". Philip Klass called the Truman memo an obvious fraud; Friedman judged the briefing paper and the memo "almost certainly genuine". The briefing paper lists "Dr. Donald Menzel" among the twelve members of the group it says Truman established in September 1947, and its page 4 says "some scientists, most notably Dr. Menzel, consider it more likely that we are dealing with beings from another solar system entirely." The tellers report the naming as the paper makes it; that Menzel served on such a panel holds only as far as the paper is genuine.

documents.title: Eisenhower briefing document (MJ-12, 1952)
documents.provenance: A typed briefing paper dated 18 November 1952, with a Truman memorandum to Secretary Forrestal of 24 September 1947 as its Attachment A, that came to light on a roll of 35mm film Jaime Shandera received anonymously at his Burbank home in 1984 and that he, William Moore and Stanton Friedman then studied; it was made public in 1987. The National Archives and the Truman and Eisenhower Libraries report their searches for it negative. The FBI's Majestic 12 file holds copies sent to it in 1988 and 1991, each marked "BOGUS" by hand, and records that the Air Force Office of Special Investigations "advised on November 30, 1988, that the document was fabricated" and that "the document is completely bogus". Philip Klass called the Truman memo an obvious fraud; Friedman judged the briefing paper and the memo "almost certainly genuine".

documents.title: Cutler-Twining memo (MJ-12, 14 July 1954)
documents.provenance: A one-page memorandum dated 14 July 1954 from Robert Cutler to General Nathan Twining that Jaime Shandera and William Moore reported finding in July 1985 in Record Group 341, Entry 267, at the National Archives. The Archives says it "poses problems": the series is filed by Top Secret register number and it bears none; its marking "Top Secret Restricted Information" came into use at the National Security Council only under Nixon; it has no letterhead or watermark; the NSC minutes hold no meeting on 16 July 1954; and Cutler was abroad on 14 July 1954. Stanton Friedman judged it "almost certainly genuine", answering that Cutler had left instructions with NSC executive secretary James Lay. The FBI's Majestic 12 file holds a copy marked "BOGUS" by hand.

documents.title: Eisenhower briefing document (MJ-12, 1952)
documents.provenance: A typed briefing paper dated 18 November 1952, with a Truman memorandum to Secretary Forrestal of 24 September 1947 as its Attachment A, that came to light on a roll of 35mm film Jaime Shandera received anonymously at his Burbank home in 1984 and that he, William Moore and Stanton Friedman then studied; it was made public in 1987. The National Archives and the Truman and Eisenhower Libraries report their searches for it negative. The FBI's Majestic 12 file holds copies sent to it in 1988 and 1991, each marked "BOGUS" by hand, and records that the Air Force Office of Special Investigations "advised on November 30, 1988, that the document was fabricated" and that "the document is completely bogus". Philip Klass called the Truman memo an obvious fraud; Friedman judged the briefing paper and the memo "almost certainly genuine".

documents.title: AMC Opinion Concerning "Flying Discs" (the Twining memo)

discussion.by: Eisenhower briefing document (MJ-12, 1952)
discussion.text: A typed briefing paper dated 18 November 1952, with a Truman memorandum to Secretary Forrestal of 24 September 1947 as its Attachment A, that came to light on a roll of 35mm film Jaime Shandera received anonymously at his Burbank home in 1984 and that he, William Moore and Stanton Friedman then studied; it was made public in 1987. The National Archives and the Truman and Eisenhower Libraries report their searches for it negative. The FBI's Majestic 12 file holds copies sent to it in 1988 and 1991, each marked "BOGUS" by hand, and records that the Air Force Office of Special Investigations "advised on November 30, 1988, that the document was fabricated" and that "the document is completely bogus". Philip Klass called the Truman memo an obvious fraud; Friedman judged the briefing paper and the memo "almost certainly genuine". The briefing paper lists "Gen. Nathan F. Twining" among the twelve members and says "A covert analytical effort organized by Gen. Twining and Dr. Bush acting on the direct orders of the President" judged the recovered disc a short range reconnaissance craft in September 1947. This is the paper behind Michels' "rumored Majestic 12", and Twining's place in the group holds only as far as it is genuine; the Twining memo he also names is the 1947 Air Materiel Command letter on flying discs, a separate document.

discussion.by: Cutler-Twining memo (MJ-12, 14 July 1954)
discussion.text: A one-page memorandum dated 14 July 1954 from Robert Cutler to General Nathan Twining that Jaime Shandera and William Moore reported finding in July 1985 in Record Group 341, Entry 267, at the National Archives. The Archives says it "poses problems": the series is filed by Top Secret register number and it bears none; its marking "Top Secret Restricted Information" came into use at the National Security Council only under Nixon; it has no letterhead or watermark; the NSC minutes hold no meeting on 16 July 1954; and Cutler was abroad on 14 July 1954. Stanton Friedman judged it "almost certainly genuine", answering that Cutler had left instructions with NSC executive secretary James Lay. The FBI's Majestic 12 file holds a copy marked "BOGUS" by hand. The memo, addressed to General Twining and dated 14 July 1954, says "The President has decid[[ed]] that the [[MJ-12]] SSP br[[ief]]ing should take place during the already sched[[ul]]ed White [[Ho]]use meeting of July 16" (double brackets mark letters illegible in the FBI's copy). It would place Twining inside an MJ-12 briefing, as the rumor Michels mentions has it; it does so only as far as the memo is genuine.

discussion.text: An unsigned report that Michael Shellenberger delivered to Congress and Rep. Nancy Mace entered into the record of the House Oversight hearing of 13 November 2024 as a document from the Pentagon; it calls itself the public version of a Defense Department employee's report, cleared for release by the State Department; Matthew Brown, a former Defense Department official, later said he wrote it; and a Defense Department spokesperson said the department has no record of a program by that name. The report's case "NORTHCOM Jellyfish UAP Crosses US-Mexico Border" says that on government networks there is FLIR footage of "an irregularly shaped UAP flying across the southern border" that "approximated a jellyfish or floating 'brain' with hanging appendages". Jesse Michels reads out the case's heading, so the story is the report's own account; the report describes the footage in words and holds no image of it.

discussion.text: Oppenheimer does not say which translation his words follow, and he read the Gita in Sanskrit; in Edwin Arnold's 1885 translation read here, Krishna's words at chapter 11, verse 32 are "Thou seest Me as Time who kills, Time who brings all to doom", the same verse in another translator's English. "Now I am become death, the destroyer of worlds" is Oppenheimer's own rendering of it, with death where Arnold has Time.

discussion.by: Critias (translated by Benjamin Jowett)
discussion.text: In Jowett's translation of the Critias, Critias counts the nine thousand years back from his own day to the war, not from Solon's visit to Egypt, and speaks of "many great deluges" during those years rather than one flood.

discussion.by: Timaeus (translated by Benjamin Jowett)
discussion.text: In Jowett's translation of the Timaeus, the 9000 years are counted by the Egyptian priest speaking to Solon ("As touching your citizens of 9000 years ago"), back to the Athenians who fought Atlantis, and the "violent earthquakes and floods" that sank the island came "afterwards"; the date of 600 BC for Solon's visit is the tellers', and the festival in the text, "the Apaturia", is where the elder Critias told the tale to the younger, generations after Solon. Matching the 9000 years to the end of the ice age and to Meltwater Pulse 1B is the tellers' step from the text's count, which the text neither states nor excludes.

stories.title: Plato's Atlantis located in Antarctica

the combatants on the other side were commanded by the kings of Atlantis, which, as I was saying, was an island greater in extent than Libya and Asia, and when afterwards sunk by an earthquake, became an impassable barrier of mud to voyagers sailing from hence to any part of the ocean.

This power came forth out of the Atlantic Ocean, for in those days the Atlantic was navigable; and there was an island situated in front of the straits which are by you called the Pillars of Heracles; the island was larger than Libya and Asia put together, and was the way to other islands, and from these you might pass to the whole of the opposite continent which surrounded the true ocean; for this sea which is within the Straits of Heracles is only a harbour, having a narrow entrance, but that other is a real sea, and the surrounding land may be most truly called a boundless continent.

discussion.by: Timaeus (translated by Benjamin Jowett)
discussion.text: In Jowett's translation of the Timaeus, the power of Atlantis "came forth out of the Atlantic Ocean" from an island "in front of the straits which are by you called the Pillars of Heracles", from which "you might pass to the whole of the opposite continent which surrounded the true ocean"; the text sets the island itself in the Atlantic before the straits, with that continent beyond it. Reading "the opposite continent" or "the true ocean" as Antarctica and the world ocean around it, and placing Atlantis there, is the teller's step, which the text neither states nor excludes.

discussion.by: Ramon Watkins (Prophet Yahweh)
discussion.text: Watkins announces in a press release that for 45 days from June 1, 2005 he will call down UFOs for the media over Las Vegas and that a spaceship will descend on his signal and sit in the sky for almost two days.

discussion.by: KTNV Channel 13 Las Vegas (reporter Mike Dello Stritto)
discussion.text: The station's crew meets Watkins at a time and place of their choosing in the last week of May 2005; two objects appear on camera, a white one and then an orange orb, and the footage runs on the evening news. The linked copy is the segment as it circulates today.

discussion.by: KVBC News 3 Las Vegas (Steve Crupi)
discussion.text: A second station tries the same thing days later from the driveway of Watkins' apartment and reports seeing only an airplane: 'We tried, it's a no-show.' The station's own page is gone; the words survive in a forum repost.

discussion.by: Richard Bartholomew
discussion.text: Bartholomew lists the explanations skeptics offered within two days (a model aircraft, a balloon, lasers, a concentrated light effect) and notes the site was near Nellis Air Force Base.

discussion.by: Guy Malone (Alien Resistance)
discussion.text: Malone says an anonymous site's weather-balloon theory has most likely 'got PY's UFOs pegged' and runs photos captioned as Watkins with weather balloons, adding that Watkins says the man in them is not him.

discussion.by: Mike Dello Stritto (as reported)
discussion.text: The reporter is quoted as having gone in expecting to ridicule the claim and come away believing he had seen an unidentified object; the station asked Nellis about aircraft and got no answer. Reported in a 2007 Wikipedia snapshot, the station's own page being gone.

discussion.by: Ramon Watkins (Prophet Yahweh)
discussion.text: Watkins says the spaceship would never have appeared if he had not been filmed calling it down, blames the Las Vegas media for refusing to film the promised descent, and demands 45 days of standby cameras.

discussion.by: Wikipedia editors (2007 snapshot)
discussion.text: The article offers as one explanation that Watkins signals a friend who releases balloons nearby during his meditation, and in the same breath calls this speculation with no evidence, since the crew chose the location.

discussion.by: Jeffery Pritchett (Church of Mabus radio)
discussion.text: Pritchett reports that Watkins' brother confirmed his death from a heart attack in August 2014, and says he is still not sure how Watkins pulled the summoning off.

discussion.by: Metabunk posters SharpEye and Duke
discussion.text: SharpEye says the first object 'is very much a white balloon'; Duke says they look like balloons and asks whether the station was complicit.

discussion.by: Metabunk poster SharpEye
discussion.text: The same poster says the second object gives him trouble: it seems to travel through the clouds and ascend vertically at speed.

discussion.by: Metabunk poster Z.W. Wolf
discussion.text: Wolf reads the orange orb as a specular reflection of the sun from a distant aircraft, a shapeless blob when the angle is right.

discussion.by: Jesse Michels
discussion.text: Michels says people have since looked at the footage and said Watkins had an associate who released a balloon, adding that there is no evidence this happened and that it is an alternative hypothesis.

discussion.by: Jeffrey Mishlove
discussion.text: Mishlove answers that alternative hypotheses are often morphing constantly and weaker than 'just the thing happened'.

tellings.quote: you know the Robertson panel in 1953 absolutely adopted this policy of ridicule
The Panel's concept of a broad educational program integrating efforts of all concerned agencies was that it should have two major aims: training and "debunking."

discussion.by: Report of Meetings of Scientific Advisory Panel on Unidentified Flying Objects (Robertson Panel), 14-18 January 1953
discussion.text: The tellers do not say which of the panel's papers they mean; in the minutes and the report read here the panel recommends an educational program with "two major aims: training and 'debunking.'", carried by "mass media such as television, motion pictures, and popular articles" and built on "case histories which had been puzzling at first but later explained", so as to bring a "reduction in public interest in 'flying saucers'", and it asks the security agencies to strip the objects of "the aura of mystery they have unfortunately acquired". That is the policy the tellers call ridicule; whether debunking through the mass media meant mocking witnesses is a step the report neither states nor excludes.

discussion.text: The panel's minutes name the "Civilian Flying Saucer Investigators" and the "Aerial Phenomena Research Organization" and say such organizations "should be watched because of their potentially great influence on mass thinking" and that "the possible use of such groups for subversive purposes should be kept in mind", an official recommendation to keep watch on named civilian groups, which is what Salas tells as "keep an eye on". The step from watched to infiltrated, which the story's name carries, is a reading the report as released neither confirms nor excludes. As context, not as evidence: how a watch was to be kept is the kind of thing such minutes rarely set down.

discussion.by: Timaeus (translated by Benjamin Jowett)
discussion.text: In Jowett's translation of the Timaeus, the old priest at Sais tells Solon that the great deeds "have all been written down by us of old, and are preserved in our temples", the temple record the teller describes, and gives him the laws himself: "I will briefly describe them to you, and you shall read the account of them at your leisure in the sacred registers". In the text the priest tells the story and the record waits to be read later; whether it stood on a wall or in registers, and the picture of priests reading hieroglyphs aloud to Solon, are the teller's details, which the text neither states nor excludes.

discussion.text: An unsigned report that Michael Shellenberger delivered to Congress and Rep. Nancy Mace entered into the record of the House Oversight hearing of 13 November 2024 as a document from the Pentagon; it calls itself the public version of a Defense Department employee's report, cleared for release by the State Department; Matthew Brown, a former Defense Department official, later said he wrote it; and a Defense Department spokesperson said the department has no record of a program by that name. The report's case "SOUTHCOM Tic-Tac Detected by Space Asset in Proximity of Vessel" describes "OPIR imagery and MASINT of a Tic-Tac UAP transiting through an area of the Atlantic Ocean" and says "No observed reaction is seen to come from the vessel", reading the vessel's nearness as a sign of "foreknowledge of the UAP event by intelligence". discussion.by: The Epic of Gilgamish, Tablet XI (translated by E. A. Wallis Budge in The Babylonian Story of the Deluge)
discussion.text: In Budge's translation of the Eleventh Tablet, the god Ea warns one man, the "man of Shurippak": "Throw down the house, build a ship", and "The dimensions thereof shall be measured"; he takes "all my family and kinsfolk" aboard with the beasts of the field, the ship comes to rest on a mountain, he sends out a dove, a swallow and a raven in turn, and after landing he offers a sacrifice and "The gods smelt the sweet savour." These are the elements the tellers set beside Noah's story, and the tablet's own names (Uta-Napishtim, the mountain of Nisir) count neither for nor against a borrowing. What the tablet alone cannot settle is which way the story travelled, whether both tellings come from an older common one, and whether a real flood is remembered in it; the comparison with Genesis is the tellers'.

discussion.by: Talking with Planets
discussion.text: In Talking with Planets, an article in Collier's Weekly in 1901, Tesla writes that at his Colorado laboratory he recorded electrical changes with "a clear suggestion of number and order" that he came to feel were "the greeting of one planet to another"; he describes hearing signals, not speaking or communicating with anyone, and writes of an answer as something still to come. The tellers do not name the writing they mean; this is the one in which Tesla describes the Colorado Springs signals.

discussion.by: INTERVIEW: D.W Pasulka brings 'American Cosmic' to the UFO forefront
discussion.text: Here Pasulka writes that Tyler "credits his ‘protocol’ with allowing him to predict outcomes, and maybe this is true, I don’t know", a protocol of "physical and mental exercises"; she keeps her own doubt beside his claim. The step from a protocol that predicts outcomes to business ideas downloaded from a non-human intelligence is the tellers' reading of the book, which this interview neither states nor excludes.

discussion.by: Immaculate Constellation report (anonymous, entered into the House Oversight hearing record, 13 November 2024)
discussion.text: An unsigned report that Michael Shellenberger delivered to Congress and Rep. Nancy Mace entered into the record of the House Oversight hearing of 13 November 2024 as a document from the Pentagon; it calls itself the public version of a Defense Department employee's report, cleared for release by the State Department; Matthew Brown, a former Defense Department official, later said he wrote it; and a Defense Department spokesperson said the department has no record of a program by that name. The report's case "INDOPACOM Intelligence Vessels Positioned to Collect on Reproduction Vehicle" has "a large equilateral-triangle UAP" appear "directly over the ships", a grouping of vessels collecting "at night in a specific area of the Pacific Ocean", whose presence it puts down to "foreign pre-positioning of advanced collection assets". That this case is the one off Kamchatka with Russian vessels comes from Matthew Brown's and Jeremy Corbell's accounts of the briefing; the report gives the place as a specific area of the Pacific and the vessels as foreign.

discussion.text: The letter's own words (paragraph 2a) are "The phenomenon reported is something real and not visionary or fictitious", which the tellers give closely. documents.provenance: A typed briefing paper dated 18 November 1952, with a Truman memorandum to Secretary Forrestal of 24 September 1947 as its Attachment A, that came to light on a roll of 35mm film Jaime Shandera received anonymously at his Burbank home in 1984 and that he, William Moore and Stanton Friedman then studied; it was made public in 1987. The National Archives and the Truman and Eisenhower Libraries report their searches for it negative. The FBI's Majestic 12 file holds copies sent to it in 1988 and 1991, each marked "BOGUS" by hand, and records that the Air Force Office of Special Investigations "advised on November 30, 1988, that the document was fabricated" and that "the document is completely bogus". Philip Klass called the Truman memo an obvious fraud; Friedman judged the briefing paper and the memo "almost certainly genuine".

discussion.by: Eisenhower briefing document (MJ-12, 1952)
discussion.text: A typed briefing paper dated 18 November 1952, with a Truman memorandum to Secretary Forrestal of 24 September 1947 as its Attachment A, that came to light on a roll of 35mm film Jaime Shandera received anonymously at his Burbank home in 1984 and that he, William Moore and Stanton Friedman then studied; it was made public in 1987. The National Archives and the Truman and Eisenhower Libraries report their searches for it negative. The FBI's Majestic 12 file holds copies sent to it in 1988 and 1991, each marked "BOGUS" by hand, and records that the Air Force Office of Special Investigations "advised on November 30, 1988, that the document was fabricated" and that "the document is completely bogus". Philip Klass called the Truman memo an obvious fraud; Friedman judged the briefing paper and the memo "almost certainly genuine". The briefing paper's page 5 says "On 06 December, 1950, a second object, probably of similar origin, impacted the earth at high speed in the El Indio - Guerrero area of the Texas - Mexican boder" ("boder" as typed), that it was almost totally incinerated, and that "Such material as could be recovered was transported to the A.E.C. facility at Sandia, New Mexico, for study." The teller places the 1950 crash where the paper does and names the paper as its main source, so the crash stands as far as the paper does; the paper says nothing of Willingham's 1955 case, which rests on other tellings.

discussion.by: The Pentagon Disinformation That Fueled America's UFO Mythology (The Wall Street Journal, 2025)
discussion.text: The article gives the EMP explanation as the finding of Sean Kirkpatrick's AARO team: "Kirkpatrick’s team dug into the story and discovered a terrestrial explanation", an Air Force "exotic electromagnetic generator" that "simulated this pulse of disruptive energy without the need to detonate a nuclear weapon", set "on a portable platform 60 feet above the facility", whose pulses "snaked down cables connected to the bunker where launch commanders like Salas sat". The tellers read this as the reporters' own explanation; in the text it is the reporters' account of what the investigators found, resting, by the article's own statement, on "interviews with two dozen current and former U.S. officials, scientists and military contractors involved in the inquiry" and documents it does not name.

discussion.by: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024 (Public Law 118-31), sections 1841 to 1843
discussion.text: An act of Congress signed into law on 22 December 2023 and printed by the Government Publishing Office as Public Law 118-31; nothing about its text is disputed. The UAP sections of the law enacted on 22 December 2023 have the Archivist set up "a collection of unidentified anomalous phenomena ... records in the National Archives", have "each head of a Government office" identify and prepare such records for it, and let disclosure be postponed on the original classification authority's finding of "clear and convincing evidence" of harm. The Senate's UAP Disclosure Act of 2023 (SA 797) had given "Witnesses, close observers, and whistleblowers providing information directly to the Review Board" the protections of 50 U.S.C. 3373b(b) through an independent Review Board, and the enacted sections set up no such board; the teller does not say which protections he means, and if they are these, the law shows the end state of the conference he calls a reconciliation, not the bargaining that led to it.

discussion.by: The Epic of Gilgamish, Tablet XI (translated by E. A. Wallis Budge in The Babylonian Story of the Deluge)
discussion.text: The teller does not say which part of the epic he means; if it is the flood of the Eleventh Tablet, the source says the great gods resolved "to make a wind-storm" and tells a rain-flood, "A black cloud from the foundation of heaven came up" in which Adad thundered, while the Anunnaki, whom the translator glosses as "The star-gods of the southern sky", "brandished their torches" and "With their glare they lighted up the land". Star-gods lighting up the land with torches is the tablet's nearest image to fire from the sky; reading the flood as the memory of an impact is a step the tablet neither states nor excludes. The words are from E. A. Wallis Budge's translation (The Babylonian Story of the Deluge, 1920) of the Eleventh Tablet of the Assyrian version, in which Uta-Napishtim tells Gilgamish of the flood.

discussion.by: The Book of Enoch (translated by R. H. Charles)
discussion.text: The teller names the Book of Enoch beside Ezekiel for its strange depictions and does not say which passage he means; if it is Enoch's first dream-vision, which the translator heads as a vision on the Deluge, the book tells how "the heaven collapsed and was borne off and fell to the earth" and "the earth was swallowed up in a great abyss" (83:3 to 4), and has Mahalalel read the dream as "the secrets of all the sin of the earth: it must sink into the abyss and be destroyed with a great destruction" (83:7). Where the book tells the flood itself it is a judgement announced to Noah, "a deluge is about to come upon the whole earth" (10:2). The book tells the destruction as a judgement for sin; reading the falling heaven as the memory of an impact at the Younger Dryas is the teller's step, which the text neither states nor excludes.

discussion.text: The epic gives Uta-Napishtim as the "man of Shurippak" and says "The mountain of Nisir held the ship", a mountain of its own name, where Genesis has the ark rest "upon the mountains of Ararat" (Genesis 8:4); placing the landing in the Ararat region follows Genesis, not the tablet. Same 1956 article and the same quote about working with nuclear fuels to cancel out gravity, but the story gives it to George Trimble and this telling gives it to Lawrence Bell.

Same subject as the German submarine uranium story: Nazi uranium on a submarine ending up in American bombs. The core claim differs: a deliberate SS deal to send it to the US, rather than a captured submarine bound for Japan.

The same early-1970s SRI test of Swann affecting a shielded device with Puthoff, but here the device is a thermistor in a Faraday cage rather than a shielded quark detector.

Both are about James Randi's paranormal challenge. The stored story claims the prize was really a 30-year payout that Randi judged himself, while this telling presents it as a straightforward cash prize that began at $10,000.
Same 1947 Roswell crash as the Jason Sands story, but this telling blames lightning, not high-powered radar, for bringing the craft down.

Kripal speaking on levitation or flying saints to a Lockheed revolutionary-technology head. This is the same subject as the story of the levitation talk to Lockheed engineers, but here it is a public MIT lecture the head attended, not a private talk he asked for.

Both are about McMoneagle remote viewing the supposed alien mountain bases that Pat Price named. Here he says they were over-the-horizon radar sites, not alien command centers.

Same 1947 Kenneth Arnold sighting, but this telling claims the craft matched the Horten brothers' design, which recasts the object as a human-built craft.

Hypnosis tapes in which Puharich himself suggests the Nine. This tells the Nine coming through under hypnosis as Puharich's leading questions rather than real contact, which is a different core claim about the same kind of session.
Same event, Leandro's discovery of the bodies, but this telling says his first version was an underground citadel or temple with stone sarcophagi, not a cave behind a collapsed wall.

Both are about Menzel and the 1953 break in Harvard Observatory sky data. This telling says he deleted the data, where the story says he stopped the survey.
Same 2024 New Jersey drone flap, but this telling claims the objects come from underwater, emerging off the coast.
Both concern what kind of evidence the Nimitz Tic Tac encounter gives. Madden treats it as testimony from reliable witnesses, while the story calls it multisensory evidence.

Both are about Byrd and Operation Highjump. Dolan reads Byrd's statement as not being about flying saucers, while the story claims the fleet met laser-shooting discs.

Both concern the claimed alien base off Point Dume (Sycamore Knoll); the story asserts a base that was erased from maps, while this telling says there was no base.
